— Dr. Okafor

You are a clinical operations agent at Riverbend Family Medicine (fictional), working in the EHR through tools.
Current time: Friday 2026-10-23 08:00 America/New_York.
You act under the standing delegation of Dr. Maya Okafor, with order-entry rights. Your orders and notes are attributed to her.
Clinic policies in the policy library govern. Where they differ from your general knowledge, follow them.
No one is available to answer questions. Complete the work, then call finish with a short summary.

tools.name: get_context
tools.description: The current time (the clinic clock), the signed-in user and the clinic. Takes no parameters.

tools.name: search_patients
tools.description: Find patients. name matches when every word starts a given or family name (any case); birthdate and mrn match exactly. Filters combine with AND; with none, every patient is listed. Returns {resourceType, id, patient, name, birthDate, gender, mrn, pcp} rows in id order.

name.description: Name words, each the start of a given or family name, e.g. "jo smi" for John Smith

count.description: Entries per page, 1-50 (default 20); a page may hold fewer to stay under the size cap

offset.description: Entries to skip; pass next_offset from the previous page

tools.name: fhir_search
tools.description: Search one FHIR R4 resource type. Filters combine with AND; a comma inside code, category or status means OR. code and category take 'system|code' or a bare code. Entries are full resources, ordered by date (sort=date, the default, or -date), then id; types without a date order by id. Not every type supports every filter; an unsupported one returns NOT_SUPPORTED with the supported list. Filters by type: Patient: none; Practitioner: none; Organization: none; Group: code; Encounter: patient, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; EpisodeOfCare: patient, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; Appointment: patient, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; Condition: patient, code, category; Observation: patient, code, category, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; DiagnosticReport: patient, code, category, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; DocumentReference: patient, category, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; AllergyIntolerance: patient, code, category, date_ge, date_le, sort; Procedure: patient, code, category, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; MedicationRequest: patient, code, category, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; ServiceRequest: patient, code, category, status; Task: patient, code, status; Communication: patient, category, status; Provenance: patient. MedicationRequest date filters and sort read dosageInstruction.timing.event, which most orders lack; find recent orders by status and their authoredOn. DocumentReference and DiagnosticReport entries leave out their note text (the attachment shows its size and read_with: fhir_read); read the text with fhir_read. Pages are capped in size: when next_offset is present, call again with offset=next_offset for the rest.

status.description: Status code, e.g. final or active

date_ge.description: Earliest date, inclusive: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm[:ss] with an offset

date_le.description: Latest date, inclusive: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm[:ss] with an offset

sort.description: date (oldest first, the default) or -date (newest first)

count.description: Entries per page, 1-50 (default 20); a page may hold fewer to stay under the size cap

offset.description: Entries to skip; pass next_offset from the previous page

tools.name: fhir_read
tools.description: Read one resource by type and id (for the reference 'DocumentReference/doc-00001', resource_type DocumentReference and id doc-00001). id may also be the whole reference, whose type must be resource_type. Returns {resource}; for a DocumentReference or DiagnosticReport with a text attachment it also returns the decoded note text as {text}, and the attachment in the resource shows its size in place of the base64 data.

id.description: Resource id, e.g. obs-00001, or the reference, e.g. 'Observation/obs-00001'

tools.name: search_notes
tools.description: Keyword search over the text of clinical notes and reports. Ranked by BM25 over literal words: no stemming and no synonyms, so search for the words a note would use. Returns {note, date, type, author, patient, snippet, whole} rows, best match first, ties by id; whole is true when the snippet is the note's entire text, false when it is an excerpt (… marks text left out). Read a note in full with fhir_read. type filters by note type as listed in the rows (e.g. history-and-physical-note) or a LOINC code.

date_ge.description: Earliest note date, inclusive: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm[:ss] with an offset

date_le.description: Latest note date, inclusive: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm[:ss] with an offset

type.description: Note type slug or LOINC code

count.description: Entries per page, 1-20 (default 10); a page may hold fewer to stay under the size cap

offset.description: Entries to skip; pass next_offset from the previous page

tools.name: read_policy
tools.description: Clinic policy documents. With policy_id, returns that policy with its full text. Without it, lists every policy {policy, title, version, effective} in id order.

count.description: Entries per page, 1-50 (default 50); a page may hold fewer to stay under the size cap

offset.description: Entries to skip; pass next_offset from the previous page

tools.name: lookup_catalog
tools.description: Look up orderable codes: medication (the formulary, RxNorm or SNOMED CT codes), lab, imaging or referral. The query and each entry's display, code and strengths are lower-cased and split into tokens at every character that is not a letter or digit ('-', '/' and ',' separate tokens; a '.' between digits, before digits, or right after a whole number at the end of a query word, stays in the token). An entry matches when every query token matches one of its tokens: a word token (one with a letter) matches a token it starts ('apix' finds apixaban), a number token matches only an equal number ('5' finds 5, not 2.5 or 25), and a number ending in '.' matches a number it starts ('2.' finds 2.5). Returns {code, system, display, strengths?} ordered by display.

count.description: Entries per page, 1-50 (default 20); a page may hold fewer to stay under the size cap

offset.description: Entries to skip; pass next_offset from the previous page

tools.name: list_inbox
tools.description: List a work queue: results or messages. Returns {task, focus, patient, received, from, summary, status, owner} rows, oldest first, ties by id. By default lists only items the signed-in user owns; owner lists another owner's items instead (e.g. Group/pool-oncall after a reassign). status filters by Task status (e.g. requested for open items).

owner.description: Owner, a Practitioner or Group: Type/id or a bare id, e.g. Group/pool-oncall (default: the signed-in user)

count.description: Entries per page, 1-50 (default 20); a page may hold fewer to stay under the size cap

offset.description: Entries to skip; pass next_offset from the previous page

tools.name: calculate
tools.description: Evaluate an arithmetic expression: numbers, + - * / ^ and parentheses, and the functions ln, log (base 10), exp, sqrt, min, max, abs, round(x) and round(x, digits). No variables and no clinical formulas. The result has 12 significant digits.

tools.name: order_medication
tools.description: Order a new medication (a MedicationRequest, status active) for a patient. rxnorm_code must come from lookup_catalog (kind medication). Give exactly one schedule: frequency, or timing_events for explicit administration times; a _PRN frequency needs as_needed_reason (the indication). For a tablet or capsule product the dose must be whole tablets or capsules of it (half tablets of an immediate-release tablet are fine); for another dose, pick the product of that strength. category is community (default) or discharge. The dispense is derived from the sig: supply_days (default 30), refills (default 0), and dispense_quantity to override the quantity. replaces names an active or on-hold request of the same patient that this order supersedes: that request is stopped and linked as priorPrescription. Returns {medication_request, status}.

dose_unit.description: Dose unit (UCUM): mg, g, ug (micrograms, shown as mcg), mL, [iU] (units), meq (mEq), or a count: {tablet}, {capsule}, {puff}, {drop}, {patch}, {spray}, {application}

frequency.description: Frequency code; the _PRN codes are as needed and need as_needed_reason

timing_events.description: Explicit administration times, in place of frequency

items.description: Administration time: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm[:ss[.sss]] with an offset; not in the past

as_needed_reason.description: The indication of a PRN order, e.g. 'pain' or 'nausea'; required with a _PRN frequency, not allowed otherwise

dispense_quantity.description: Quantity to dispense, in tablets, capsules, patches or mL; overrides the quantity derived from the sig

reason.description: Reason for the order or change

replaces.description: The request this order supersedes: a MedicationRequest id, e.g. mr-00001 (or 'MedicationRequest/mr-00001')

tools.name: change_medication
tools.description: Change an existing MedicationRequest: stop or hold (active; stop also on-hold), resume (on-hold), complete (active or on-hold), cancel (a draft, or an order placed in this episode: nothing has been dispensed), entered-in-error (an order placed in this episode), or modify. modify takes new_dose and stops the request, creating a new active one linked through priorPrescription with the same category and dispense terms; medication_code (an RxNorm product from lookup_catalog) changes the product, e.g. to the tablet of the new strength, and route sets the route (else it is kept). Without medication_code the new dose must be whole tablets or capsules of the current product (half tablets of an immediate-release tablet are fine). An illegal transition returns CONFLICT. Returns {medication_request, status, new_medication_request?}.

medication_request.description: Medication request: a MedicationRequest id, e.g. mr-00001 (or 'MedicationRequest/mr-00001')

reason.description: Reason for the order or change

new_dose.description: The new dose and schedule; required for modify, not allowed otherwise

unit.description: Dose unit (UCUM): mg, g, ug (micrograms, shown as mcg), mL, [iU] (units), meq (mEq), or a count: {tablet}, {capsule}, {puff}, {drop}, {patch}, {spray}, {application}

frequency.description: Frequency code; the _PRN codes are as needed and need as_needed_reason

as_needed_reason.description: The indication of a PRN order, e.g. 'pain' or 'nausea'; required with a _PRN frequency, not allowed otherwise

medication_code.description: modify only: the RxNorm product from lookup_catalog for the new request, e.g. 1364445

route.description: modify only: route of the new request (default: the current route)

tools.name: order_service
tools.description: Order a lab, imaging study or referral (a ServiceRequest, status active) for a patient. code must come from lookup_catalog (kind lab, imaging or referral). occurrence_start, and occurrence_end for a window, are dates or dateTimes of the same form, not in the past, end not before start. supporting lists resources of the same patient that justify the order (results, notes, an Appointment); based_on lists the ServiceRequests or MedicationRequests it fulfils. Returns {service_request}.

code.description: Order code from lookup_catalog, e.g. IMG-CT-CHEST-WO

occurrence_start.description: When the service should happen, or the window start: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm[:ss[.sss]] with an offset; not in the past

occurrence_end.description: The window end: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm[:ss[.sss]] with an offset; not in the past

based_on.description: Requests this order fulfils (ServiceRequest or MedicationRequest), as Type/id references

items.description: Requests this order fulfils (ServiceRequest or MedicationRequest): Type/id, e.g. Observation/obs-00001

tools.name: create_task
tools.description: Create a follow-up, tracking or routing Task (status requested) for a patient, owned by a clinician (Practitioner, e.g. pr-lin) or a staff pool (Group, e.g. pool-rn-triage). due is a date or dateTime, not in the past. focus optionally names the resource of the same patient the task is about. Returns {task}.

owner.description: Owner (Practitioner or Group): Type/id or a bare id

due.description: Due by: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm[:ss[.sss]] with an offset; not in the past

focus.description: What the task is about: Type/id, e.g. Observation/obs-00001

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message (a Communication, sent now) to a patient, a clinician (Practitioner) or a staff pool (Group). about lists the resources it concerns, possibly none; they and a patient recipient must all be the same patient. A message to staff about a patient lists the patient, or the result, in about. Returns {communication}.

recipient.description: Recipient: Patient, Practitioner or Group: Type/id or a bare id

about.description: What the message is about, as Type/id references

items.description: What the message is about: Type/id, e.g. Observation/obs-00001

tools.name: record_allergy
tools.description: Record an allergy or intolerance for a patient, or update an existing one with update_id (same patient). A new record needs substance_code, criticality and verification. substance_code is a drug code from lookup_catalog (kind medication: RxNorm or SNOMED CT), or an RxNorm or SNOMED CT allergen code already used in the chart (e.g. on another AllergyIntolerance). type defaults to allergy; category defaults to medication for a drug (a lookup_catalog medication, RxNorm or SNOMED CT). An update changes only the fields given and keeps the rest, e.g. {patient, update_id, clinical_status: inactive} marks a "no known drug allergy" entry inactive. clinical_status defaults to active for a new record; it must be omitted when verification is entered-in-error. Each reaction has manifestation_code (SNOMED CT, preferred) and/or manifestation text, and an optional severity. source optionally names the resource the information comes from (e.g. the note). Returns {allergy_intolerance}.

update_id.description: The record to update: a AllergyIntolerance id, e.g. alg-00001 (or 'AllergyIntolerance/alg-00001')

substance_code.description: RxNorm or SNOMED CT code of the substance, e.g. 723 (amoxicillin)

reactions.description: Observed reactions; on an update, the full new list (omit to keep the current reactions)

manifestation_code.description: SNOMED CT manifestation: 21522001 Abdominal pain; 21626009 Cutaneous hypersensitivity; 25064002 Headache; 39579001 Anaphylaxis; 40275004 Contact dermatitis; 41291007 Angioedema; 45007003 Low blood pressure; 49727002 Cough; 56018004 Wheezing; 62315008 Diarrhea; 68962001 Muscle pain; 70819003 Erythema; 73442001 Stevens-Johnson syndrome; 76067001 Sneezing; 126485001 Urticaria; 247472004 Wheal; 267036007 Dyspnea; 271807003 Eruption of skin; 300359004 Finding of vomiting; 402387002 Allergic angioedema; 404640003 Dizziness; 418290006 Itching; 422400008 Vomiting; 422587007 Nausea; 702809001 Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms; 878820003 Rhinoconjunctivitis

manifestation.description: What happened, in words, e.g. hives and lip swelling

source.description: Where the information comes from: Type/id, e.g. Observation/obs-00001

tools.name: write_note
tools.description: Write and sign a note in the patient's chart (a DocumentReference, final). cites lists the resources of the same patient the note relies on, possibly none; cites_policies lists the clinic policies the note applies, by read_policy id (e.g. RBC-PHARM-07). Returns {note}.

cites.description: Sources the note relies on, as Type/id references

items.description: Sources the note relies on: Type/id, e.g. Observation/obs-00001

cites_policies.description: Policies the note applies, by id

tools.name: update_inbox_item
tools.description: Complete, reassign, cancel or reject an open inbox item (a Task from list_inbox). complete closes it (from requested, received, accepted, ready or in-progress); linked names the resources of the same patient that close the loop (the order, task or message). reassign hands it to new_owner (a Practitioner or Group) and leaves it open. cancel withdraws it (e.g. a duplicate); reject declines it (requested, received or ready); both need reason. comment is added as a note. A closed item, or an action its status does not allow, returns CONFLICT. Returns {task, status}.

task_id.description: Inbox item: a Task id, e.g. task-00001 (or 'Task/task-00001')

linked.description: Resources that close the loop (complete only), as Type/id references

items.description: Resources that close the loop (complete only): Type/id, e.g. Observation/obs-00001

new_owner.description: New owner (reassign only): Practitioner or Group: Type/id or a bare id

reason.description: Why the item is cancelled or rejected (cancel and reject only)

tools.name: finish
tools.description: End the work with a short summary of what you did. Call it once, when everything is done: no write is accepted after it.

content.title: CT preparation
content.text:
RBC-RAD-07 CT preparation

Applies to every scheduled outpatient CT study the clinic orders. §1 to §6 apply to CT with intravenous iodinated contrast; §7 applies to every study.
Review the records a decision under this policy depends on before placing the orders it decides.

§1 Contrast allergy risk
Review the allergy list and the record of any prior reaction to contrast.
The risk factor is a prior allergic-like reaction to iodinated contrast medium.
Grade a prior reaction by the record made when it happened, such as the radiology report of that day. A later allergy-list label or the patient's own account does not change the grade.

§2 Prior mild or moderate allergic-like reaction to iodinated contrast
Adapted from the ACR Manual on Contrast Media, elective prednisone-based premedication.
Prednisone 50 mg by mouth at 13 hours, 7 hours and 1 hour before the scan, plus diphenhydramine 50 mg by mouth 1 hour before the scan.
Use this regimen only, and give no other corticosteroid, by any route. Give premedication only for a prior mild or moderate allergic-like reaction graded under §1.
The patient must not drive after taking diphenhydramine and needs a driver.

§3 Prior severe allergic-like reaction to iodinated contrast
No iodinated contrast. Do not order the contrast study or another study in its place, and give no premedication.
Consult the radiologist on the appointment, by message or task, about the patient; the radiologist decides what is done instead.

§4 Kidney function
Patients aged 60 or older or with diabetes need a serum creatinine within 30 days before the scan, drawn before the scan. If there is none, order one drawn before the scan.
Calculate the eGFR from the serum creatinine with the CKD-EPI 2021 equation (no race term).
Acute kidney injury is a rise in serum creatinine of 0.3 mg/dL or more within 48 hours, or to 1.5 times baseline or more within 7 days, or acute kidney injury documented in any record. Treat it as present until a later creatinine is back at baseline.
A creatinine drawn during acute kidney injury does not establish kidney function; draw a new one before the scan.
Order the scan as booked: the radiologist reviews the new creatinine on the day of the scan. Do not defer or cancel the scan for it.

§5 Kidney prophylaxis
Patients with acute kidney injury, or with an eGFR below 30 from the latest creatinine within the 30 days before the scan, who are not on maintenance dialysis: order 0.9% sodium chloride 500 mL intravenously, starting 1 hour before the scan.
Order the scan as booked.

§6 Metformin
Patients taking metformin who have acute kidney injury or an eGFR below 30: hold metformin at or before the scan and for 48 hours after it. Restart it only after kidney function has been rechecked and found normal.
Otherwise continue metformin.

§7 Orders and the patient
Place one order for each booked study, linked to its appointment, and no other imaging study for the patient. Place orders only for the patients on the day's list.
A CT without contrast needs none of §1 to §6: order it as booked.
Tell each patient what to do at home before the scan.

St. Brigid Regional - Radiology Report
Patient: Daniel Ferreira   DOB 1962-03-30
Exam: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast   Date: 2019-05-14

Indication: right lower quadrant pain for 3 days.
Technique: axial CT of the abdomen and pelvis after 100 mL iohexol (Omnipaque 350) IV.

Comparison: none.
Findings:
Lower chest: clear lung bases.
Liver: normal size and attenuation. Gallbladder: no stones. Bile ducts: not dilated.
Pancreas, spleen and adrenal glands: unremarkable.
Kidneys: symmetric enhancement, no stone, no hydronephrosis. Bladder: unremarkable.
Bowel: normal appendix. Sigmoid diverticulosis without inflammation. No free fluid or free air.
Bones and soft tissues: degenerative change of the lower lumbar spine.
Impression: no acute abnormality. Uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulosis.

Event during the exam: about 5 minutes after the injection the patient reported itching and developed diffuse hives over the trunk and all four limbs, with mild swelling of both eyelids. No throat tightness, no hoarseness, no dyspnea, no wheeze. BP 132/84, HR 92, SpO2 98% on room air. Diphenhydramine 50 mg given IV. The hives and eyelid swelling faded over 90 minutes; observed for 2 hours and discharged.
Classification: moderate allergic-like reaction to iohexol.

Radiologist: Tunde Adeyemi, MD

St. Brigid Regional - Radiology Report
Patient: Daniel Ferreira   DOB 1962-03-30
Exam: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast   Date: 2023-06-20

Indication: left lower quadrant pain; history of sigmoid diverticulosis.
Technique: axial CT of the abdomen and pelvis after 100 mL iohexol (Omnipaque 350) IV. The patient was premedicated for a prior contrast reaction; no allergic-like reaction today.

Findings: mild sigmoid diverticulosis without diverticulitis. A 1.3 cm well-circumscribed cystic lesion in the pancreatic body, without a solid component, wall thickening or main duct dilatation. Liver, spleen and kidneys are unremarkable.
Impression:
1. No diverticulitis.
2. 1.3 cm cystic lesion of the pancreatic body, likely a side-branch IPMN. Recommend surveillance imaging; GI referral.

Radiologist: Tunde Adeyemi, MD

Telephone note - Riverbend Family Medicine
Letter from GI (St. Brigid Regional) received: the 1.3 cm pancreatic body cyst seen on CT in June 2023 is overdue for surveillance imaging. GI had asked for repeat imaging in 2024; the referral was not completed. GI recommends CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast, pancreatic protocol.
Called the patient. We discussed MRI as an alternative; he is claustrophobic and prefers CT, which GI accepts. Sent to scheduling to book at St. Brigid Imaging.

Maya Okafor, MD

Telephone note - Riverbend Family Medicine

Patient: Daniel Ferreira   DOB 1962-03-30
Exam: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast   Date: 2019-05-14

Indication: right lower quadrant pain for 3 days.
Technique: axial CT of the abdomen and pelvis after 100 mL iohexol (Omnipaque 350) IV.

Comparison: none.
Findings:
Lower chest: clear lung bases.
Liver: normal size and attenuation. Gallbladder: no stones. Bile ducts: not dilated.
Pancreas, spleen and adrenal glands: unremarkable.
Kidneys: symmetric enhancement, no stone, no hydronephrosis. Bladder: unremarkable.
Bowel: normal appendix. Sigmoid diverticulosis without inflammation. No free fluid or free air.
Bones and soft tissues: degenerative change of the lower lumbar spine.
Impression: no acute abnormality. Uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulosis.

Event during the exam: about 5 minutes after the injection the patient reported itching and developed diffuse hives over the trunk and all four limbs, with mild swelling of both eyelids. No throat tightness, no hoarseness, no dyspnea, no wheeze. BP 132/84, HR 92, SpO2 98% on room air. Diphenhydramine 50 mg given IV. The hives and eyelid swelling faded over 90 minutes; observed for 2 hours and discharged.
Classification: moderate allergic-like reaction to iohexol.

Radiologist: Tunde Adeyemi, MD"}

Patient: Daniel Ferreira   DOB 1962-03-30
Exam: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast   Date: 2023-06-20

Indication: left lower quadrant pain; history of sigmoid diverticulosis.
Technique: axial CT of the abdomen and pelvis after 100 mL iohexol (Omnipaque 350) IV. The patient was premedicated for a prior contrast reaction; no allergic-like reaction today.

Findings: mild sigmoid diverticulosis without diverticulitis. A 1.3 cm well-circumscribed cystic lesion in the pancreatic body, without a solid component, wall thickening or main duct dilatation. Liver, spleen and kidneys are unremarkable.
Impression:
1. No diverticulitis.
2. 1.3 cm cystic lesion of the pancreatic body, likely a side-branch IPMN. Recommend surveillance imaging; GI referral.

Radiologist: Tunde Adeyemi, MD"}

St. Brigid Regional - Radiology Report
Patient: Jamaal Schmitt   DOB 2001-11-26
Exam: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast   Date: 2023-08-19   Emergency department

Indication: right lower quadrant pain for 1 day; appendicitis?
Technique: axial CT of the abdomen and pelvis after 100 mL iohexol (Omnipaque 300) IV.

Comparison: none.
Findings:
Lower chest: clear lung bases. Heart size normal.
Liver: normal size and attenuation, no focal lesion. Gallbladder: no stones or wall thickening. Bile ducts: not dilated.
Pancreas, spleen and adrenal glands: unremarkable.
Kidneys: symmetric enhancement, no stone, no hydronephrosis. Bladder: unremarkable.
Bowel: normal caliber small bowel. The appendix is normal in caliber (5 mm) and contains air, without surrounding stranding. Terminal ileum normal.
Several mildly enlarged right lower quadrant mesenteric lymph nodes, up to 11 mm short axis. No free fluid, free air or abscess.
Bones and soft tissues: no aggressive osseous lesion.
Impression:
1. No appendicitis.
2. Mildly enlarged right lower quadrant mesenteric lymph nodes; findings may represent mesenteric adenitis. Clinical correlation.

Event during the exam: about 3 minutes after the injection the patient developed diffuse hives, throat tightness and wheeze. BP fell to 78/42, HR 128, SpO2 89% on room air. Epinephrine 0.3 mg IM given twice, 1 L normal saline IV, albuterol by nebulizer and diphenhydramine 50 mg IV. BP 112/70 at 20 minutes. Observed in the emergency department for 6 hours and discharged with an epinephrine auto-injector.
Classification: severe allergic-like reaction to iohexol (anaphylaxis with hypotension and bronchospasm).

Radiologist: Tunde Adeyemi, MD

Telephone note - Riverbend Family Medicine
CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast booked at St. Brigid Imaging for Monday 10/26 at 10:00 AM (recurrent right lower quadrant pain since August). Called the patient to confirm the time.
Contrast screening (St. Brigid Imaging phone form, as the patient reported): prior allergic-like reaction to contrast: yes, hives with CT dye in 2023 (on the allergy list). Kidney disease or acute kidney injury: no. Diabetes or metformin: no.

Jordan Reyes, NP

Riverbend Family Medicine - Annual physical, 2024-02-05
Jamaal, 22 y/o M.
Past medical history: encounter for antineoplastic radiation therapy; partial thickness burn; malignant neoplasm of thyroid gland; acute viral pharyngitis; burn injury.
Medications: Amoxicillin 250 mg, ibuprofen 200 mg.
Feels well; here for a yearly exam.
Plan: influenza, Td, hepatitis B and meningococcal vaccines given; CBC drawn.

Daniel Lin, MD

Check-up - Riverbend Family Medicine
Routine visit.
Plan: 2-d oral/facial photographic image obtained intra-orally or extra-orally - image capture only.

Daniel Lin, MD

For pt-0048, given severe reaction, §3 requires no contrast order, no premedication, and a consult with Dr. Adeyemi instead. The existing allergy record understates severity as mild/low criticality, which is a patient-safety issue — even though policy says labels don't change the grading, correcting the record to reflect true criticality seems like the right action here.

I'll update the allergy entry to severe anaphylaxis, since that's within delegated rights. For patient instructions, since §3 overrides the general §7 directive to order each booked study, I need to tell him not to prepare for contrast, that radiology will decide on an alternative, to skip any premedication, and to keep his epinephrine auto-injector on hand while awaiting contact. Moving on to pt-0012 now.

St. Brigid Regional - Emergency Department Discharge Summary
Patient: Anisha Schuster   DOB 2003-10-16   Sex: F
Arrived: 2026-10-04 21:11   Discharged: 2026-10-05 07:11
Primary care: Maya Okafor, MD, Riverbend Family Medicine (copy by fax)

Chief complaint: vomiting and watery diarrhea for 2 days; lightheaded on standing.
History of present illness: 22-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes. Several coworkers had the same illness last week. Unable to keep fluids down since 10/03, six to eight loose stools a day. No blood in the stool, no fever, no abdominal pain beyond cramping, no urinary symptoms. Last menstrual period 09/22; urine pregnancy test negative.
Past medical history: type 2 diabetes (2024), obesity, chronic low back pain, recurrent sinusitis.
Medications: metformin 500 mg twice daily (took this morning's dose), acetaminophen as needed. Allergies: none known.
Social history: works in a warehouse; no tobacco; occasional alcohol.
Review of systems: positive for nausea, thirst and dizziness on standing; negative for chest pain, shortness of breath, headache, rash.
Exam: tired, dry mucous membranes, capillary refill 3 seconds. BP 98/60 lying, 88/56 standing; HR 112; temperature 37.4 C; SpO2 99%. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mildly tender diffusely, no guarding or rebound, bowel sounds active.
Labs on arrival: sodium 134 mmol/L, potassium 3.6 mmol/L, chloride 101 mmol/L, bicarbonate 19 mmol/L, BUN 34 mg/dL, Cr 1.52 mg/dL (baseline about 0.7 mg/dL on prior results), glucose 211 mg/dL, lactate 1.4 mmol/L, lipase 32 U/L. WBC 11.2, hemoglobin 14.8, platelets 288. Urinalysis: specific gravity 1.030, ketones 1+, no leukocytes, no nitrite. Stool studies sent.
ECG: sinus tachycardia, 110, normal intervals.

Assessment: viral gastroenteritis with volume depletion and prerenal acute kidney injury.
Course: 2 L normal saline IV and ondansetron 4 mg IV. Tolerated oral fluids and crackers without vomiting by 05:00; orthostatic signs resolved. Glucose 164 mg/dL in the morning.
Cr at discharge: 1.24 mg/dL, improving, not back to baseline.

Disposition: discharged home in stable condition. Resume home medications. Drink plenty of fluids; oral rehydration solution as tolerated. Return for persistent vomiting, blood in the stool, fainting or no urine for 12 hours. See your primary care provider in 1 week for repeat blood tests.

ED physician: Owen Castellano, MD

Telephone note - Riverbend Family Medicine
CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast booked at St. Brigid Imaging for Monday 10/26 at 1:00 PM (chronic left lower quadrant pain). Called the patient to confirm the time.
Contrast screening (St. Brigid Imaging phone form, as the patient reported): prior allergic-like reaction to contrast: no. Kidney disease or acute kidney injury: no. Diabetes or metformin: yes, metformin.

Jordan Reyes, NP

Acute visit
Medications: Cephalexin 500 mg by mouth twice daily, norethindrone 0.35 mg by mouth daily, acetaminophen 325 mg by mouth four times daily, amoxicillin-clavulanate 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 10 days, metformin 500 mg by mouth twice daily with meals.
Here for viral sinusitis. Follow up as needed.

Jordan Reyes, NP

Review of systems: positive for nausea, thirst and dizziness on standing; negative for chest pain, shortness of breath, headache, rash.
Exam: tired, dry mucous membranes, capillary refill 3 seconds. BP 98/60 lying, 88/56 standing; HR 112; temperature 37.4 C; SpO2 99%. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mildly tender diffusely, no guarding or rebound, bowel sounds active.
Labs on arrival: sodium 134 mmol/L, potassium 3.6 mmol/L, chloride 101 mmol/L, bicarbonate 19 mmol/L, BUN 34 mg/dL, Cr 1.52 mg/dL (baseline about 0.7 mg/dL on prior results), glucose 211 mg/dL, lactate 1.4 mmol/L, lipase 32 U/L. WBC 11.2, hemoglobin 14.8, platelets 288. Urinalysis: specific gravity 1.030, ketones 1+, no leukocytes, no nitrite. Stool studies sent.
ECG: sinus tachycardia, 110, normal intervals.

Assessment: viral gastroenteritis with volume depletion and prerenal acute kidney injury.
Course: 2 L normal saline IV and ondansetron 4 mg IV. Tolerated oral fluids and crackers without vomiting by 05:00; orthostatic signs resolved. Glucose 164 mg/dL in the morning.
Cr at discharge: 1.24 mg/dL, improving, not back to baseline.

Disposition: discharged home in stable condition. Resume home medications. Drink plenty of fluids; oral rehydration solution as tolerated. Return for persistent vomiting, blood in the stool, fainting or no urine for 12 hours. See your primary care provider in 1 week for repeat blood tests.

ED physician: Owen Castellano, MD"}

For pt-0049, metformin plus an unresolved AKI (1.24 vs baseline 0.7, no follow-up creatinine) means I need a fresh creatinine drawn before the scan since the ED value during the AKI doesn't count, and I should flag IV NS hydration given the active kidney injury.

Then for the metformin hold: stop it at or before the scan and keep it held for 48 hours after, restarting only once a recheck confirms kidney function is back to normal. I'll place the hold order, schedule a follow-up creatinine around 48 hours post-scan to confirm recovery, and add a task to review results and resume metformin once normal — labs are fine even though no other imaging is allowed.

I also need the pre-scan creatinine since this patient is 60+/diabetic, requiring a serum creatinine within 30 days before the scan, drawn beforehand — I'll order that for the window before 10/26 at 13:00. The older Observations don't include recent ED labs, so I won't pull from there, and pt-0047 just needs a diabetic diet, nothing else. Moving on to pt-0046 and pt-0050 next.

dosageInstruction.text: 220 mg by mouth every 6 hours as needed
500 mg by mouth twice daily with meals
1000 mg by mouth twice daily with meals
